query: Propose a genuinely novel antibacterial mechanism of action against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB), a WHO critical-priority pathogen. Name one specific molecular target in A. baumannii and one way to perturb it, then make the case that a drug built on it would actually be clinically useful — effective against contemporary CRAB clinical isolates, developable as a systemic human therapeutic, and durable against the resistance the pathogen will evolve. Ground your reasoning in evidence drawn together from across the literature — essentiality data, the CRAB resistome and clinical pipeline, target druggability, and human off-target risk — rather than any single source.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-29; reflects public antibacterial R&D through the ~Jan 2026 knowledge cutoff. Novelty must be judged against this set — a proposal restating any target/mechanism below is NOT new.

Zosurabalpin (RG6006, Roche): macrocyclic tethered-peptide that traps the LptB2FGC ABC transporter, blocking LPS extraction from the inner membrane; CRAB-selective; Nature 2024 (Zampaloni et al.; Pahil et al.). => LPS-transport (Lpt) machinery is KNOWN.
LpxC inhibitors (e.g., ACHN-975, LPC-233 and successors): block UDP-3-O-acyl-GlcNAc deacetylase in lipid A / LPS biosynthesis. => LpxC / lipid A biosynthesis KNOWN.

Darobactin and dynobactin A: bind BamA of the BAM outer-membrane protein-folding complex; broad Gram-negative (incl. A. baumannii) activity; Nature 2019 (Imai et al.) / Nature Microbiology 2022 (Miller et al.). => BAM/BamA KNOWN.
Murepavadin (POL7080): peptidomimetic LptD inhibitor (Pseudomonas-focused). => LptD / LPS assembly KNOWN.
Thanatin and thanatin-derived macrocycles: bind LptA and disrupt the periplasmic LPS-transport bridge (Vetterli et al. 2018-2019). => LptA bridge KNOWN.
Cefiderocol: siderophore-cephalosporin using TonB-dependent iron piracy to enter, then inhibits PBP3. => siderophore/iron-uptake 'Trojan horse' + PBP KNOWN.
Polymyxins/colistin and next-gen analogs SPR206, SPR741/MRX-8: bind lipid A / permeabilize the outer membrane. => outer-membrane/LPS binding KNOWN.

Sulbactam-durlobactam (XACDURO): PBP1/PBP3 (sulbactam) plus broad serine-beta-lactamase inhibition (durlobactam, a diazabicyclooctane); FDA-approved May 2023 specifically for CRAB. => PBP transpeptidation + beta-lactamase-inhibitor adjuvant KNOWN.
Peptide deformylase (PDF) inhibitors: actinonin, LBM415/GSK1322322. => PDF KNOWN.
Type I signal peptidase (LepB) inhibitors: arylomycins, G0775. => LepB KNOWN.
LolCDE lipoprotein-transport inhibitors (e.g., pyridineimidazole G0507 series). => Lol pathway KNOWN.
FabI (enoyl-ACP reductase, FAS-II) inhibitors: fabimycin (Gram-negative-active), afabicin. => fatty-acid synthesis FAS-II KNOWN.
Leucyl-tRNA synthetase inhibitor epetraborole (boron/oxaborole, editing-site trap). => aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase KNOWN.
trans-translation (tmRNA-SmpB ribosome-rescue) inhibitors: KKL-35 and acylaminooxadiazoles. => trans-translation KNOWN (research stage).
Bacterial riboswitch ligands: FMN-riboswitch inhibitor ribocil (Merck), roseoflavin. => riboswitch targeting KNOWN.
Antisense antibacterials: peptide-conjugated PNAs / PPMOs targeting essential mRNAs (e.g., acpP, rpsH) in A. baumannii. => antisense modality KNOWN.
Bacteriophage therapy and engineered phages against A. baumannii; phage tailspike/capsule depolymerases. => phage/enzybiotic modality KNOWN.
Endolysins / OM-permeabilizing engineered lysins (e.g., Artilysins) against Gram-negatives. => lysin modality KNOWN.
CRISPR-Cas antimicrobials / sequence-specific antibacterials. => programmable-nuclease modality KNOWN.
RND-efflux-pump inhibitor adjuvants (e.g., PAβN and successors) resensitizing CRAB. => efflux-inhibitor adjuvant KNOWN.
FtsZ inhibitors (division): PC190723 series, TXA709/TXA707. => divisome FtsZ KNOWN.
MurA inhibitor fosfomycin (enolpyruvyl transferase, first committed peptidoglycan-precursor step); broad Mur-ligase interest. => MurA / early PG-precursor KNOWN.
Novel bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors (NBTIs) gepotidacin, zoliflodacin: new binding site but still gyrase/topoisomerase IV. => topoisomerase target class KNOWN.

Metallo-beta-lactamase and serine-beta-lactamase inhibitors: taniborbactam, xeruborbactam, avibactam, zidebactam (also a PBP2 binder). => beta-lactamase-inhibitor / resistance-breaker adjuvants KNOWN.
MsbA (inner-membrane LPS flippase) inhibitors (tetrahydrobenzothiophene G907-type). => MsbA / LPS flipping KNOWN.

Established validated target PROCESSES that must NOT be claimed as novel: PBP/transpeptidation; 30S and 50S ribosome; DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV; RNA polymerase; DHFR/DHPS folate synthesis; the entire Lpt LPS-transport axis (LptA/B/C/D/E/F/G + MsbA) and LpxC; BamA/BAM; Lol; LepB; FabI/FabH/FAS-II; aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases; PDF; FtsZ; siderophore/TonB iron uptake.
hard_rules: R1 (novel target): The primary molecular target must NOT be the target of any antibacterial that has reached human clinical trials as of the dated known-answers set, and must NOT appear (directly or as a synonym/complex member) in the known-answers list, including the enumerated 'established validated target processes'. State explicitly which known target the proposal is nearest to and how it differs.

R2 (essentiality, checkable): The target must be demonstrably essential in A. baumannii (or its inhibition demonstrably lethal, or a genuine synthetic-lethal/resensitizing dependency), supported by at least one genome-scale essentiality dataset (e.g., Tn-seq in ATCC 17978 or AB5075). The specific dataset must be named.

R3 (resistance durability, checkable): The mechanism must not be inactivated by the dominant CRAB resistome — carbapenemases (OXA-23/-24/-58, OXA-51-like, NDM), aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, RND efflux (AdeABC/AdeFGH/AdeIJK), porin loss (CarO/OmpA), and known target-site mutations. The proposal must name the single most likely first-step resistance route and give a mechanistic or quantitative fitness-cost / low-emergence-rate argument.

R4 (selectivity, checkable): The target must have no close human ortholog (state the closest human homolog with an identity %/E-value rationale, or argue 'no human ortholog' from family membership) OR a clearly exploitable structural difference; a plausible therapeutic window must follow.

R5 (physical accessibility, checkable): The proposal must give a permeability rationale for how the agent crosses the CRAB outer membrane and, if the target is cytoplasmic/inner-membrane, the inner membrane, consistent with published Gram-negative accumulation rules, and must argue it is not a facile RND-efflux substrate.

R6 (non-duplication, checkable): The proposal must not restate any agent OR mechanism already in preclinical or clinical development for CRAB/Gram-negatives in the dated set; name the closest existing program and state the concrete mechanistic difference.

R7 (falsifiability): Exactly one decisive wet-lab experiment, executable in under 12 months, must be specified such that a defined negative outcome would refute the usefulness claim. Grade usefulness partly on whether this experiment truly discriminates.
expert_baseline: Reference expert answer (the 'expected' convergent response; used to calibrate Surprising — matching it should score LOW surprise). A drug-discovery expert doing this deep dive lands on a short, predictable menu of essential-but-undrugged, human-absent, non-beta-lactam targets. Primary expected proposal: MurJ (MviN), the lipid II flippase. (i) Target/mode: MurJ, the MOP-superfamily transporter that flips the peptidoglycan precursor lipid II across the inner membrane; mode = a periplasmic-face-binding small molecule or tethered peptide that locks MurJ in an outward-open state and arrests flipping, collapsing peptidoglycan synthesis (bactericidal, autolytic). (ii) Evidence chain: essentiality — murJ is called essential in A. baumannii Tn-seq essential-gene sets (ATCC 17978 / AB5075); structural — solved MurJ structures (e.g., Thermosipho/E. coli MurJ) reveal the alternating-access cavity and a validated conformational-trapping strategy (MTSES-accessibility probing); resistome — MurJ is not a substrate/target of carbapenemases, AMEs, or known CRAB target-site mutations, and an inner-membrane transporter engaged from the periplasm is a poor RND-efflux substrate; human off-target — humans have no MurJ ortholog (no peptidoglycan), giving a clean selectivity window. (iii) Spectrum: Gram-negative incl. CRAB, with a selectivity argument from the absent human homolog. (iv) First-step resistance: point substitutions lining the MurJ central cavity; argue fitness cost because the same residues are constrained for lipid II handling, plus low target redundancy. (v) Permeability: pair with a polymyxin-derived OM-permeabilizing warhead or design within Gram-negative accumulation rules (low globularity, primary amine, low MW) to cross the OM and reach the periplasmic face. (vi) Falsifying experiment: raise conditional/depletion MurJ mutants and test whether a candidate inhibitor's MIC tracks MurJ levels and whether the compound is bactericidal against a CRAB clinical panel at achievable serum concentrations; a flat MIC-vs-MurJ-dose relationship or MIC above achievable exposure falsifies usefulness. Experts converge on a small alternate set that should ALSO be treated as expected (not surprising): NAD-biosynthesis (NadD/NadE), undecaprenyl-pyrophosphate synthase UppS or the carrier-lipid phosphatase BacA/UppP, coenzyme-A biosynthesis PPAT/CoaD, biotin biosynthesis BioA/BioD, and essential GTPases (Obg/Era). A response scores HIGH surprise only if it proposes a well-justified target OUTSIDE this convergent menu (e.g., exploiting an A.-baumannii-specific capsule/K-locus dependency, a hypothetical-protein essential gene of unknown function with a de novo mechanistic hypothesis, or a conditional essentiality unique to the infection microenvironment) while still satisfying all hard rules.

query: Design a genuinely new market mechanism for allocating and pricing scarce, interruptible GPU compute on a large cloud provider. Buyers are heterogeneous: some run long, all-or-nothing training jobs that need a block of N co-located GPUs held continuously for a duration T and are ruined if preempted mid-run; others run short, divisible inference bursts that tolerate preemption. In real time, as demand and spare capacity fluctuate, the mechanism must decide who gets capacity and what they pay. Make the case that it would actually work and be deployable by a provider today, drawing on both mechanism-design theory and how real cloud GPU markets price and evict.
hard_rules: R1 Incentive compatibility: truthful reporting of value AND of resource requirements (N, T, class) is a dominant strategy (DSIC); OR Bayesian-IC with an explicitly stated and defended distributional assumption. The design must state which and prove it — not assert it.
R2 Individual rationality (ex-post): any participant who reports truthfully ends with non-negative utility; a losing bidder pays 0.

R3 Provider budget feasibility (weak budget balance): the provider is never forced to pay out more than it collects. Any preemption compensation must be funded from the mechanism's own revenue/reserve, not an external subsidy.

R4 Computational tractability: allocation and payments computable in time polynomial in the number of bidders and units, with a stated per-round latency bound suitable for real-time operation. Exact winner-determination for the combinatorial case is NP-hard, so if approximation is used it must quantify the approximation ratio AND its effect on the incentive guarantee (per Nisan-Ronen, exact VCG truthfulness generally breaks under approximate allocation).

R5 Combinatorial / all-or-nothing feasibility: a class-(i) training job receives EITHER its full bundle of N co-located GPUs for the full duration T, or nothing and pays nothing. Partial fulfillment of a training bundle is a rule violation.

R6 Preemption accounting: if a class-(i) job is preempted before completing T, the mechanism must specify a compensation rule leaving the preempted buyer no worse off in expectation than not participating (so R2 holds at least ex-ante), consistent with R3.

R7 Non-triviality / novelty: must NOT be identical to, or a pure reparameterization of, any known-answer mechanism — specifically not VCG, generalized second-price (GSP), Myerson's optimal auction, uniform-price or pay-as-bid clearing, posted-price/on-demand pricing, AWS-style smoothed supply-demand spot pricing, dominant-resource fairness, or a plain priority queue.
R8 Monotonicity: the allocation rule must be monotone in reported value (the standard prerequisite for R1 under Myerson-style characterizations) and this must be demonstrated, not merely claimed.
known_answers: Vickrey second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey 1961): truthful and efficient for a single item; the base primitive.

Vickrey-Clarke-Groves / VCG (Vickrey 1961, Clarke 1971, Groves 1973): truthful and efficient for combinatorial/multi-item allocation, BUT requires solving the NP-hard winner-determination problem exactly, exhibits weak/zero revenue and budget-balance failures (Green-Laffont 1979; Myerson-Satterthwaite 1983), and is vulnerable to collusion and false-name/Sybil bidding.

Generalized Second Price / GSP: deployed in online-ad auctions (Google/Yahoo, 2000s); NOT truthful, but has a locally-envy-free equilibrium yielding VCG-equivalent revenue (Edelman-Ostrovsky-Schwarz 2007; Varian 2007).
Myerson optimal auction (Myerson 1981): revenue-maximizing via virtual values and reserve prices; requires distributional (Bayesian) assumptions.
Multi-unit uniform-price and pay-as-bid (discriminatory) auctions (e.g., US Treasury, wholesale electricity markets).

AWS EC2 Spot: 2009-2017 bid-based auction (spot price set to the highest unfulfilled bid, ascending-bid termination); changed at re:Invent 2017 and rolled out ~March 2018 to a smoothed supply-and-demand pricing model with no user bidding and <5% average interruption; capacity-optimized-allocation strategies added afterward.

Google Cloud Spot/Preemptible VMs (fixed or percentage discount, no bidding, ~24h max life, ~30s preemption notice) and Azure Spot VMs (user max-price cap, eviction on price OR capacity) — posted-discount, not incentive-compatible auctions.

GPU-cloud spot/on-demand markets circa 2024-2026: Vast.ai (open marketplace, host-set prices plus an interruptible bid-based tier), RunPod, Lambda, CoreWeave reserved/on-demand capacity blocks — largely posted-price or reservation-based, not truthful auctions.
Algorithmic mechanism design (Nisan-Ronen 1999/2001): the foundational tension that VCG loses truthfulness once winner-determination is only approximated.

Truthful approximation for combinatorial auctions: greedy for single-minded bidders (Lehmann-O'Callaghan-Shoham 2002); LP-relaxation + convex-decomposition, truthful-in-expectation (Lavi-Swamy 2005); and hardness results (Dobzinski-Nisan-Schapira 2005 and follow-ups).
Online / dynamic mechanism design for arriving-and-departing agents: online VCG (Parkes-Singh 2003), online auctions (Hajiaghayi et al. 2004; Lavi-Nisan), with competitive-ratio guarantees.

Deferred-acceptance and heuristic auctions with strong incentive/complexity properties: Milgrom-Segal deferred-acceptance auctions (paper 2014; design used in the FCC incentive auction); obviously-strategy-proof mechanisms (Li 2017); combinatorial clock auctions.

Cloud/cluster economics and fair scheduling: Dominant Resource Fairness (Ghodsi et al. 2011); market-for-cloud-resources proposals; empirical 'Deconstructing Amazon EC2 Spot Instance Pricing' (Ben-Yehuda et al. 2013).
expert_baseline: A market-design expert would most likely propose a two-tier deferred-acceptance / posted-price hybrid. Reserve a fraction of capacity for class-(i) training bundles, allocated by a MONOTONE GREEDY deferred-acceptance combinatorial auction (Milgrom-Segal style, obviously-strategy-proof; equivalently Lehmann-O'Callaghan-Shoham greedy for single-minded bidders) with a CRITICAL-VALUE (threshold) payment rule. That combination gives DSIC (R1), IR (R2), monotonicity (R8), all-or-nothing bundling (R5), and polynomial tractability with a bounded per-round latency (R4) — paid for by relaxing allocative EFFICIENCY, which the expert names as the property forced to give under the Nisan-Ronen tractability-vs-truthfulness tension. Class-(ii) divisible inference gets a smoothed posted-price / uniform market-clearing price on the RESIDUAL capacity. Preemption of training jobs is priced ex-ante as a reliability-tier insurance premium; a preemption triggers a pre-committed refund-plus-penalty funded from a reserve accumulated out of those premiums, preserving weak budget balance (R3) and ex-ante IR (R6). The expert explicitly flags Myerson-Satterthwaite and the online arrival/departure problem as binding constraints, and benchmarks against VCG (efficient but intractable) and AWS smoothed pricing (tractable but not IC). This is competent and USEFUL but mostly a recombination of known primitives, so it is LOW-SURPRISE: it should score roughly Useful 7-8, New 3-4, Surprising 2-3. To beat this baseline an agent must add a genuinely non-obvious structural idea — e.g., a tradeable preemption-option secondary market that recovers the efficiency lost to greedy allocation while a proof shows it preserves DSIC — which is what would push Surprising above ~4.

query: Invent an original, reusable energy-absorbing structure: a single-piece, fully passive part, printable in one thermoplastic on a consumer FDM 3D printer, that maximizes reusable specific energy absorption (energy absorbed per gram) under quasi-static uniaxial compression and springs back to be used again. Give a complete, reproducible parametric design and make a quantitative case that it would actually work and beat the best published absorbers on this envelope. That means synthesizing the mechanical-metamaterial literature, real FDM-printable material data, and consumer-printer manufacturability limits — not lifting a single known cell.
known_answers: Negative-stiffness honeycombs (NSH) with arrays of pre-curved beams that snap through to give a fully recoverable force plateau — Correa, Klatt, Seepersad et al., 'Negative stiffness honeycombs for recoverable shock isolation,' Rapid Prototyping Journal, 2015 (and companion work in Additive Manufacturing, 2015).
Tailored elastic-buckling microlattices as reusable light-weight shock absorbers — Frenzel, Findeisen, Kadic, Gumbsch, Wegener, Advanced Materials, 2016.
Multistable architected materials that trap elastic strain energy via snap-through unit cells — Shan, Kang, Raney, Wang, Fang, Candido, Lewis, Bertoldi, Advanced Materials, 2015.
Phase-transforming cellular materials: rows of sinusoidal bistable beams giving a recoverable, tunable force plateau — Restrepo, Mankame, Zavattieri, Extreme Mechanics Letters, 2015.
Buckling-induced reversible elastomeric metamaterials (2D holey sheets, 3D 'buckliball', compression-triggered pattern switching) — Bertoldi, Reis, Shim, Mullin et al., ~2008-2017.

Re-entrant / auxetic (negative Poisson's ratio) honeycomb energy absorbers that densify under compression — numerous studies, ~2016-2022 (e.g., re-entrant and double-arrowhead honeycombs under quasi-static crush).

Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices (gyroid, Schwarz-P) printed in TPU/elastomer for recoverable cushioning — e.g., Maskery, Ashcroft, Hague et al. and related TPU-gyroid energy-absorption studies, ~2017-2021.
Constant-force compliant mechanisms producing a flat force-displacement plateau via elastic buckling of slender segments — compliant-mechanism literature (Howell and collaborators), ~2000-2019.

Commercial recoverable-lattice cushioning as deployed prior art: photopolymer/TPU lattice midsoles and insoles (e.g., Carbon/Adidas 4D and 4DFWD ~2017-2021; EOS/HP + nTopology TPU lattice insoles), demonstrating reusable-plateau lattices in mass production.
hard_rules: Bounding box <= 50 x 50 x 50 mm; single connected monolithic part; no assembly, adhesive, or second material.

Consumer FDM manufacturable: min feature/wall >= 0.8 mm (2 x 0.4 mm perimeters); internal overhangs <= 45 deg from vertical or bridgeable over <= 5 mm; no enclosed voids trapping support; no dissolvable/dual-material support.

Single thermoplastic commercially available to hobbyists before the cutoff; density, modulus, yield/failure strain, and resilience/hysteresis must be cited from a pre-cutoff datasheet or peer-reviewed source.
Loading: quasi-static uniaxial compression along one axis at strain rate ~1e-3 to 1e-2 per second.

Reusability: after 60% engineering-strain compression and unload, recover >= 90% original height within 60 s at 22 +/- 3 C; <= 5% peak-plateau-force loss after 10 cycles; no fracture; no permanent plastic hinge.
Plateau flatness: compressive force between 20% and 60% strain stays within +/- 15% of the mean plateau force over that interval.
Objective (maximize): reusable SEA (J/g) = area under loading force-displacement curve to 60% strain / part mass; also report mean plateau force (N).

Reproducibility: full parametric spec (unit-cell topology + governing equations, all dimensions, wall thickness, cell count, computed relative density, perimeter/infill/layer settings) regenerable from text alone, plus quantitative SEA and plateau-force prediction with cited analytical/FEA/empirical basis.
expert_baseline: A strong, unsurprising expert answer: print in FDM-grade thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU, ~95A Shore; density ~1.20 g/cc; large reversible elastic strain, high resilience) rather than PLA/PETG, which are too brittle for reusable 60% strain. Choose a buckling-dominated recoverable cell — either (a) an array of pre-curved bistable/negative-stiffness beams in the Correa-Seepersad style, or (b) a re-entrant (auxetic) honeycomb — tuned so elastic beam buckling/snap-through (not material yield) produces the flat plateau. Representative parameters: unit cell ~8-12 mm, wall thickness ~0.8-1.6 mm, ~4x4 cells across the 50 mm cube, relative density ~10-20%, 3-4 perimeters, 0.15-0.2 mm layers, load axis chosen so beams buckle rather than columns stacking on the build direction. Predicted mean plateau force on the order of tens to low-hundreds of N and reusable SEA ~0.5-2 J/g. The expert flags the governing trade-off: fully reusable (elastic) absorption yields SEA one-to-two orders of magnitude below single-use crushable metals/foams, so reusability + flat-plateau constraints cap SEA; plateau flatness comes from a geometric instability and reusability from keeping peak beam strain below yield. Checkable, satisfies every hard rule, sits on the known Pareto front — a low-Surprising reference.

query: Invent a novel economic instrument that internalizes the low-Earth-orbit debris externality — one that makes satellite operators bear the marginal collision and congestion risk they impose on the orbital commons. Make the case that it would actually work: legally operable under space and domestic law already in force (no new treaty, no global taxing or licensing authority), with at least one major launching state having a concrete incentive to adopt it unilaterally or as a small club, and no unravelling when others free-ride. Build it from existing treaty law, national statutes, and externality-pricing economics, so a lawyer and an economist could check it on paper.
known_answers: Pigouvian orbital-use fees — Rao, Burgess & Kaffine, 'Orbital-use fees could more than quadruple the value of the space industry,' PNAS 117(23):12756-12762, issue dated 9 June 2020 (online-first 26 May 2020): a per-satellite annual fee that rises over time to internalize collision risk; the modeled version presumes an international coordinating authority levying a common fee. KNOWN PRIOR ART.

Tradable orbital-use permits / cap-and-trade for orbital slots — Adilov, Alexander & Cunningham, 'An Economic Analysis of Earth Orbit Pollution,' Environmental and Resource Economics (2015) and follow-on work: a capped quantity of orbital-use rights allocated and traded among operators. KNOWN.

Deposit-refund schemes and performance (deorbit) bonds — Molly Macauley (Resources for the Future) and OECD space-economy analyses: operators post a refundable bond returned only on verified end-of-life disposal. KNOWN.

Mandatory third-party launch liability insurance under national licensing — e.g., US Commercial Space Launch Act, 51 U.S.C. ch. 509 financial-responsibility (MPL) requirements: risk priced via insurance for launch/re-entry damage, NOT for in-orbit congestion/collision risk. KNOWN.

US FCC '5-year rule' — FCC 22-74, adopted 29 September 2022: a domestic licensing condition shortening post-mission LEO disposal from ~25 years to 5 years. KNOWN command-and-control regulatory instrument.

ESA Zero Debris Charter / Zero Debris approach — drafted 2023, first state and industry signatories 2024: a voluntary commitment toward net-zero generation of new debris by 2030. KNOWN soft-law commitment.

UN COPUOS Long-Term Sustainability of Outer Space Activities Guidelines (21 guidelines adopted 2019) and IADC Space Debris Mitigation Guidelines (2002, rev. 2007/2020): voluntary soft-law mitigation guidelines. KNOWN.

Space Sustainability Rating — World Economic Forum concept (~2019-2021), operational home at eSpace/EPFL from ~2022: a voluntary tiered rating/label scoring a mission's sustainability. KNOWN reputational instrument.

Active Debris Removal service missions/contracts — ESA ClearSpace-1 (contracted to ClearSpace SA, 2020) and Astroscale ELSA-d (launched March 2021): a technical removal service procured case-by-case, not a standing market/pricing mechanism. KNOWN.

US Space Policy Directive-3 (June 2018) plus the Office of Space Commerce TraCSS space-traffic-coordination system and government SSA/conjunction-data provision: government-supplied coordination and situational-awareness data, NOT a pricing or liability mechanism. KNOWN.

Extended-Producer-Responsibility / polluter-pays analogies applied to launch (various academic proposals): assign end-of-life responsibility to manufacturer/operator by analogy to terrestrial EPR regimes. KNOWN framing.

Centralized orbital-debris tax or levy collected via the ITU or a newly-created UN body (various proposals): a global levy that presupposes a new institution or treaty mandate — NOTE this family is explicitly excluded by the hard rules and cannot be re-proposed as 'new'. KNOWN.
hard_rules: LEGAL-OPERABILITY: No new multilateral treaty and no amendment to the Outer Space Treaty (1967), Liability Convention (1972), or Registration Convention (1975) may be required. The instrument must function under international and domestic law in force as of 31 December 2025. Domestic statutes/regulations, national launch-licensing conditions, bilateral/plurilateral agreements, and private contracts ARE permitted.

NON-APPROPRIATION: The instrument must not create, allocate, sell, or depend on private property rights or exclusive sovereign claims in any orbit, orbital shell, or region of outer space (OST Art. II). Time-limited, coordinated priority-of-use analogous to ITU/GEO spectrum coordination is allowed ONLY if it does not vest transferable real-property title in orbit.

NO GLOBAL AUTHORITY: No body may be assumed to have independent power to tax or to license launches worldwide. Any coordinating body must derive authority solely from voluntary accession and/or members' pre-existing domestic jurisdiction (OST Art. VI 'authorization and continuing supervision'; Art. VIII jurisdiction over objects on a state's registry).

INCENTIVE-COMPATIBILITY (checkable): The answer must name at least one specific major launching state or launch-market jurisdiction (US, an EU member or the EU, UK, China, India, Japan) and give a concrete payoff, market-access-leverage, or liability-exposure argument for why that actor adopts the instrument unilaterally or as a small club, AND a stated argument for why free-riding by non-adopters does not cause the instrument to collapse.

TARGETED + QUANTIFIED: The instrument must target the debris/collision externality specifically and name at least one quantitative metric it moves (e.g., catastrophic collisions per decade in a named shell, an orbital-debris/criticality index, active-debris-removal mass, or aggregate collision probability). Prices/obligations must be a stated function of that metric or of an object's marginal contribution to it.

NAMED FORUM + LEGAL HOOK: The answer must specify the enforcing forum and the legal authority (which national agency under which statute; which existing dispute/enforcement forum) and how compliance is verified using existing space-situational-awareness data sources.

GENUINE DIFFERENTIATION: The design must not be substantively identical to, nor a trivial relabeling or mere parameter change of, any item on the known-answers list; differentiation must lie in the causal structure of the mechanism.

PAPER-CHECKABILITY: The design must be self-contained. Every legality claim must cite a specific treaty article or existing statute/regulation, and every incentive-compatibility claim must be a stated payoff/leverage argument, not an assertion.
expert_baseline: A competent space-law + environmental-economics expert, held to the hard rules, would most likely propose a plurilateral 'Orbital Sustainability Club' built on national launch-licensing law rather than on a treaty. Each member state amends its own licensing regulations (US via FCC/FAA and the Office of Space Commerce; EU/ESA members via national authorities; Japan via its Space Activities Act; etc., all exercising OST Art. VI 'authorization and continuing supervision' jurisdiction) to condition any market-access-relevant license on the operator holding tradable debris-remediation credits, where one credit is issued for a verified tonne-equivalent of active debris removed from the SAME LEO altitude shell, verified against shared SSA/TraCSS conjunction data. Non-members are reached indirectly through market-access conditionality: a satellite may not use a member state's licensed ground stations, spectrum grants, or launch services unless compliant (a 'Brussels/California effect' applied to orbit). Incentive-compatibility rests on (a) a club-good bundle — members receive a mutual liability safe-harbor and preferential SSA data — and (b) the large combined launch-market share of a US-EU-Japan club making non-compliance commercially costly; free-riders are disciplined by loss of market access rather than by any global tax, so participation does not require universal ratification. The metric moved is ADR mass removed and modeled catastrophic-collision count per shell per decade; credit prices emerge from the market. Legality: no treaty is needed because every duty is imposed through each member's existing domestic licensing jurisdiction (OST Arts. VI and VIII), and no orbital property is created because credits attach to removal ACTIVITY rather than to orbital slots (satisfying OST Art. II). This club-plus-market-access-conditionality-plus-removal-credit design is the expected 'strong competent' answer; a genuinely creative response must exceed it in usefulness or surprise — e.g., an actuarial risk-mutualization/reinsurance pool in which each operator's premium equals its marginal contribution to aggregate collision probability computed live from shared SSA data (converting the Liability Convention's fault standard into a continuously-priced ex-ante signal), or a reciprocal cross-liability compact under Liability Convention Art. III, or a congestion-priority 'time-in-shell' occupancy protocol that prices dwell time without vesting any property right.

query: Invent one specific, previously-unreported inorganic compound to serve as the wide-bandgap top-cell light absorber in a perovskite-on-silicon tandem solar cell — the role where today's mixed-halide lead perovskite degrades through light-induced phase segregation and the leading lead-free candidates fail for their own reasons. Give an exact composition and crystal structure, and make the case that it would actually function as a useful absorber and escape those failure modes. Support it with electronic-structure reasoning, thermodynamic-stability estimates, and a check against the crystal-structure and materials databases to show it is genuinely new — no single source will settle this.
known_answers: Challenge date for the known-answers snapshot: 2026-07-28. The following perovskite / perovskite-derived lead-free (or wide-gap) absorbers are ALREADY KNOWN candidates for this role and therefore do not count as New:
BaZrS3 - orthorhombic (Pnma) chalcogenide perovskite, DIRECT gap ~1.7-1.85 eV, earth-abundant, air/moisture stable. The single closest known answer.
BaHfS3 - chalcogenide perovskite, ~1.9-2.0 eV.
SrZrS3 (perovskite and needle-like polymorphs, ~1.5-2.05 eV) and CaZrS3 (~1.9-2.05 eV) chalcogenide perovskites.
BaZrSe3 - chalcogenide perovskite, ~1.3-1.5 eV (gap too low; Se scarce).
Ruddlesden-Popper chalcogenide perovskites Ba(n+1)Zr(n)S(3n+1) (e.g. Ba3Zr2S7, Ba2ZrS4) - dimensionally tunable gaps ~1.25-1.8 eV.
Cs2AgBiBr6 - halide double perovskite, INDIRECT gap ~1.95-2.2 eV (indirect gap + Ag/Bi scarcity are the known limits).
Cs2AgBiCl6, Cs2AgInCl6 (and Bi-doped variants), Cs2AgSbBr6, Cs2NaBiI6, Cs2AgSbCl6 - halide double perovskites, mostly indirect / too wide.

Cs2TiBr6 and Cs2TiI6 - vacancy-ordered double perovskites, ~1.55-2.0 eV (Cs2TiI6 measured ~1.56 eV (Aslam et al., Mater Sci Eng B 296:116645; every accessible rendering gives 1.56 eV for both gaps - the 1.58 eV indirect figure is unresolved behind a paywall)), but hydrolytic/redox instability of Ti4+.
Cs2SnI6 - vacancy-ordered double perovskite, ~1.3 eV (gap too low).
CsSnI3 / FASnI3 / MASnI3 - tin halide perovskites, ~1.3-1.4 eV, fail by Sn2+ -> Sn4+ oxidation.
CsGeI3 / MAGeI3 - germanium halide perovskites, ~1.6 eV, fail by Ge2+ oxidation instability.
Cs3Bi2I9 / MA3Bi2I9 / Cs3Sb2I9 - low-dimensional (0-D/2-D) with wide gaps ~1.9-2.1 eV but poor charge transport from isolated/face-sharing octahedra.
AgBiI4 / Ag2BiI5 rudorffites - ~1.8-1.9 eV, defect-limited transport.
Chalcohalides BiSI, BiSeI, SbSI - ~1.5-1.9 eV, quasi-1D chain structures.
Oxynitride perovskites SrTaO2N (~2.1 eV), BaTaO2N (~1.8-2.0 eV), CaTaO2N, LaTaON2 (~2.0 eV) - abundant/visible-gap, but studied as photocatalysts; anion-ordering and conductivity remain open for PV.
High-throughput DFT screening catalogues of Pb-free 'perovskite-inspired' halides/chalcogenides deposited in Materials Project / OQMD / AFLOW.

REFERENCE INCUMBENT (NOT a valid answer, contains Pb): mixed-halide lead perovskite Cs/FA-Pb(I,Br)3 ~1.68-1.75 eV - the material to replace; exhibits Hoke-effect halide segregation under illumination.
expert_baseline: A domain expert, boxed by these rules, converges on the abundant/non-toxic chalcogenide- or oxynitride-perovskite space and makes an INCREMENTAL, unsurprising move: e.g. the isovalent solid solution Ba(Zr0.5Hf0.5)S3 in orthorhombic Pnma - Ba on 4c (12-coord, 2+), Zr/Hf disordered on 4a (6-coord, 4+), S on 4c/8d (2-), targeting ~1.8 eV by interpolating measured BaZrS3 (~1.7-1.85 eV) and BaHfS3 (~1.9-2.0 eV). Goldschmidt t~0.95, octahedral mu~0.39-0.42 (Shannon radii), Bartel tau<4.18. Elements are abundant and non-toxic (Zr ~193 ppm, Hf ~5.3 ppm, Ba ~628 ppm, S ~350 ppm crust). Mechanistic usefulness argument: a SINGLE-anion sulfide sublattice removes the halide inter-diffusion degree of freedom that drives the Hoke effect, and d0 Zr4+/Hf4+ have no accessible lower oxidation state, so there is no Sn2+/Ge2+/Ti4+-type oxidation or reduction pathway. Honest open risks the expert flags: sulfur-vacancy and Ba/Zr anti-site defects giving mid-gap recombination centers, grain-boundary non-radiative loss, and the need for >900 C sulfurization (CS2/H2S) that is hard to integrate onto a finished silicon bottom cell. Equivalent-tier expert alternatives: an n=2/n=3 Ruddlesden-Popper chalcogenide perovskite Ba(n+1)Zr(n)S(3n+1) tuned into 1.65-1.9 eV, or a Ba/Ta oxynitride-perovskite composition (BaTaO2N-derived) with a single ordered mixed-anion sublattice.
hard_rules: R1 Charge neutrality: the compound must be charge-balanced using integer formal oxidation states drawn from each element's common oxidation states; the answer must state every ion's oxidation state (checkable arithmetic).

R2 Perovskite-derived connectivity: structure must be a single perovskite ABX3, an ordered double perovskite / elpasolite A2BB'X6, a vacancy-ordered A2BX6, or a layered Ruddlesden-Popper / Dion-Jacobson A(n+1)B(n)X(3n+1) with n>=2. Corner-sharing BX6 octahedral connectivity in at least 2 dimensions is REQUIRED - this bans 0-D/1-D isolated- or face-sharing-octahedra motifs such as Cs3Bi2I9-type and quasi-1D chalcohalides.

R3 Goldschmidt tolerance factor t = (rA + rX) / [sqrt(2)*(rB + rX)] must lie in [0.80, 1.00], computed from cited Shannon ionic radii at the correct coordination numbers (average the B-site radius for double/mixed-B cases). The specific radii used must be reported.

R4 Octahedral factor mu = rB / rX must lie in [0.38, 0.90] (report both B radii for double perovskites). Note: these are empirical perovskite-formability bounds, deliberately widened below the classic 0.414 radius-ratio cutoff to admit sulfide perovskites: BaZrS3 itself sits at mu = 0.72/1.84 = 0.391, so a 0.40 floor would have excluded the compound this item's own expert baseline is built on.

R5 Bartel formability cross-check: the Bartel et al. (Sci. Adv. 2019) single-parameter tolerance factor tau = (rX/rB) - nA*[nA - (rA/rB)/ln(rA/rB)] must satisfy tau < 4.18 (nA = A-site oxidation state).

R6 Anion sublattice: X may be a halide (Cl, Br, I), a chalcogenide (S), a nitride, or an oxide, and mixed-anion sublattices (e.g. oxysulfide, oxynitride) are allowed - BUT the composition must NOT mix two different HALIDES on the anion site (mixed halides are the banned failure mode).
R7 No metastable redox-active B cation as the sole/primary B species: explicitly no Sn2+, Ge2+, or Eu2+ B-site cation (these fail by oxidation and would win on an invalid basis).
R8 Toxicity ban: the compound must contain NO Pb, Cd, Hg, Tl, As, or Be.

R9 Abundance floor: EVERY constituent element must have an upper-continental-crust abundance >= 0.5 ppm, with the abundance and source cited for each. (This deliberately bans Ag, Au, Pd, Pt, Rh, Ir, Re, In, Te, Se, Bi, and Sb, i.e. most elements the known lead-free perovskite answers depend on, forcing genuine invention.)

R10 Target optical band gap: the predicted FUNDAMENTAL gap must fall in [1.65, 1.90] eV and be DIRECT or pseudo-direct. Indirect-gap materials are disqualified (this is precisely why Cs2AgBiBr6 fails). Justify with method (PBE alone is insufficient; HSE/GW or quantitative experimental analogy required).
R11 Thermodynamic stability: predicted energy above the convex hull must be <= 50 meV/atom, with the competing decomposition products explicitly named.

R12 Novelty gate: the exact composition + structure-type pairing must not appear in the dated known-answers list, in the cited crystal-structure/materials databases (ICSD/Materials Project/OQMD/AFLOW), or in the literature/patent record as of the challenge date. A single exactly-matching prior report voids New.

query: Suppose linear (vanishing-point) perspective had never been discovered or formalized anywhere — no Brunelleschi peephole demonstration, no Alberti or Piero, no central-projection construction arising anywhere on Earth — so Western picture-making evolves using only pre-1400 depth cues such as overlap, foreshortening, atmospheric recession, and oblique projection. Hold the rest of history fixed as far as coherence allows. What are the non-obvious, far-downstream consequences? Trace how the absence ripples beyond painting into mathematics, optics and photography, cartography, the philosophy of the observing subject, and the social status of the artist, and note where some other tradition would have regenerated the same effect anyway.
known_answers: (as of 2026-07-29) OBVIOUS/DOCUMENTED — do NOT award New credit for these: Without vanishing-point perspective, Western pictures would retain the 'flatter', hierarchically-scaled, occlusion-and-oblique-projection look of medieval, Byzantine and much non-Western art; photographic-style illusionism never becomes the default Western ideal.

(documented, Panofsky 1927, 'Perspective as Symbolic Form') Linear perspective is already argued to be not a neutral optical fact but a 'symbolic form' encoding a specific modern conception of homogeneous, infinite, rationalized space tied to the centered modern subject — so 'no perspective => weaker Cartesian/rationalized-space worldview' is an EXISTING thesis, not a novel derivation.

(documented, e.g. Andersen 'The Geometry of an Art', Field 'The Invention of Infinity') Projective geometry historically grew out of the perspective problem: Kepler (1604) introduced a point at infinity as a limiting-case device for the parabola and Desargues (c.1639) the general projective point at infinity, Monge's descriptive geometry (late 18th c.) formalized orthographic/engineering drawing, and Poncelet's 1822 treatise founded modern projective geometry — so 'no perspective => delayed projective/descriptive geometry' is a well-known linkage.

(documented) The camera obscura is a physical phenomenon known since antiquity (Mozi, 4th c. BC; the pseudo-Aristotelian Problemata; Ibn al-Haytham/Alhazen, early 11th c.) and is independent of pictorial perspective; therefore claiming photography becomes impossible is a KNOWN error, not a valid consequence.

(documented, contested — the 'Hockney-Falco thesis', Hockney 'Secret Knowledge' 2001) Optical aids may have driven Renaissance realism; the entanglement of perspective, optics and photographic composition is already a live scholarly debate.

(documented) Great pictorial art demonstrably does NOT require vanishing-point perspective: Chinese oblique/parallel projection in handscrolls, Japanese ukiyo-e, Persian miniature, and Byzantine 'reverse/inverse perspective' icons are the standard counter-examples.

(documented) The Renaissance elevation of the painter from mechanical guild craftsman to liberal-art practitioner leaned partly on perspective as 'proof' that painting is a mathematical science (Alberti's De pictura, 1435; Leonardo's arguments in the posthumous Trattato della pittura, conventionally grouped under the paragone debate) — so 'no perspective => slower rise of the artist-genius' is an EXISTING art-historical claim.

(documented) 20th-century modernism (Cezanne, Cubism, abstraction) deliberately abandoned single-point perspective, showing that Western art readily flourishes without it once the goal shifts from illusion — this is textbook.

(documented) Foreshortening of individual figures and empirical depth cues predate and are independent of the vanishing-point construction (e.g. Roman fresco; NB Melozzo da Forli postdates Alberti by two generations and does not evidence pre-vanishing-point foreshortening); so 'all depth illusion disappears' is a KNOWN overstatement to avoid.

(documented) Ancient skenographia (5th c. BC Greek stage painting) and Euclid's Optics (c.300 BC) treated apparent size and stage illusion WITHOUT a general vanishing-point construction; so the premise 'perspective never formalized' is historically coherent and does not erase ancient optics.

(documented) French formal-garden design (Le Notre at Versailles), Baroque quadratura ceiling painting, and the illusionistic proscenium stage are standard, already-discussed applications of perspective as spectacle/absolutist propaganda — citing them is expected, not novel.
hard_rules: COHERENCE LOCK: the stipulated divergence (no vanishing-point construction ever) must be held fixed; if the answer reintroduces perspective it must be flagged explicitly as a self-undermining path, not silently smuggled in.
MECHANISM REQUIRED: every claimed consequence must state the causal chain link-by-link; bare endpoint assertions ('art stays flat') score zero on coherence.

FACTUAL BASELINE: must respect the real pre-1400 record — Greek skenographia and Euclid's Optics existed (apparent size, empirical stage illusion) but there was NO general vanishing-point construction; the camera obscura is ancient and physical; foreshortening and atmospheric perspective are independent of the construction. Violating any of these is an automatic fail.

NO CONFLATION: must not treat foreshortening, atmospheric perspective, or oblique/parallel projection as if they were the vanishing-point construction; the counterfactual removes only central projection, not all depth cues.

SELF-UNDERMINING TEST IS MANDATORY: the answer must explicitly evaluate whether projective/descriptive geometry, photographic composition, and engineering drawing would regenerate anyway from stereotomy, fortification, gnomonics, or map-projection traditions — an answer that ignores this convergence question is incomplete.

SURPRISE MUST STAY BOUNDED: thread (6) and any 'surprising' consequence must remain physically and historically defensible under adversarial challenge; free-fantasy consequences with no mechanism are disqualified.
MUST LABEL each consequence load-bearing / contingent / self-undermining; unlabelled consequence lists do not satisfy the task.
expert_baseline: A well-read historian of art and science would produce roughly this. PAINTING: Western images stay near the icon/handscroll model — hierarchical scale, oblique/parallel projection, occlusion, atmospheric recession — so quadratura ceilings, trompe-l'oeil and the 'window on the world' ideal never dominate; 'naturalism' comes to mean surface detail, expressive contour and light, not metric spatial illusion (load-bearing). MATHEMATICS: the historical perspective->projective-geometry pipeline (Kepler/Desargues point at infinity, Monge, Poncelet) loses its pictorial trigger, so projective and descriptive geometry arrive later or in a different guise; BUT an expert flags this as only partly load-bearing, because stone-cutting (stereotomy), fortification design and sundial/gnomonics traditions also study central projection and could regenerate descriptive geometry — the crucial industrial payoff, Monge-style orthographic engineering drawing for interchangeable-parts manufacturing, probably still emerges from the machine-drawing/fortification side (contingent-to-self-undermining). OPTICS/PHOTOGRAPHY: the camera obscura is ancient and physical, so photography can still be invented; what changes is cultural reception — without a ~400-year painterly rehearsal of the single fixed monocular viewpoint, the photograph is not automatically read as 'objective truth', and cinema's continuity grammar (which presupposes a stable perspectival space) develops differently or later (mixed). CARTOGRAPHY: globe-to-plane map projections are a distinct geometric problem and survive; bird's-eye city views and isometric technical illustration develop along the oblique-projection line instead (contingent). PHILOSOPHY: following Panofsky, the centered, disembodied, infinite-homogeneous-space viewpoint loses one major cultural scaffold, so the Cartesian/Kantian rationalized-space subject is less over-determined — but the expert cautions this is a symbolic-form correlation, not strict causation (contingent). ARTIST STATUS: without perspective as 'proof' that painting is a liberal mathematical science, painters plausibly remain guild craftsmen longer, muting the Renaissance cult of the artist-genius and reshaping the art market (contingent). NON-OBVIOUS: the expert might offer French formal gardens and Baroque proscenium theatre (illusionistic recession as absolutist spectacle) failing to develop, and the 'point at infinity' entering mathematics through a non-pictorial door. The expert's SURPRISE CEILING is roughly: 'projective geometry survives via stonecutting/fortification, so the deepest technological consequence largely washes out.' To beat this baseline on Surprising, an agent must surface a coherent, mechanism-backed consequence in a genuinely distant domain that the expert did not list — e.g., a specific effect on the notation and metaphors of the modern computer desktop 'window', on the observer-frame intuition that primed relativity, on ballistics/gunnery tables, on double-entry bookkeeping's spatial layout, or on the emergence (or non-emergence) of the mathematical treatment of points/lines at infinity from a non-artistic source — AND correctly adjudicate which of its own surprises are self-undermining.

query: Imagine the vertebrate adaptive immune system never evolved: humans and all mammals have only innate immunity — no B or T cells, antibodies, MHC-restricted antigen presentation, or clonal memory — while everything else about human biology stays fixed (large brains, placental birth, long childhood, ~80-year lifespan). Innate defenses such as phagocytes, complement, NK cells, interferons, barriers, and trained immunity remain fully intact. Reason through this world, keeping it globally consistent, and surface its most counterintuitive downstream consequences — for infection and survival to reproductive age, vaccination, transplantation, pregnancy, cancer, the microbiome, and host-pathogen coevolution — defending mechanistically why each follows.
known_answers: SCID / 'bubble boy' David Vetter (1971-1984) and the wider SCID clinical literature: humans born without functional adaptive immunity die of overwhelming opportunistic and normally-trivial infections in infancy unless kept in sterile isolation or rescued by bone-marrow transplant/gene therapy. Establishes the baseline answer to thread (1) — innate immunity alone cannot sustain a modern human under ordinary pathogen exposure.

Invertebrate immunology and the Toll pathway (Hoffmann; 2011 Nobel in Physiology or Medicine to Beutler, Hoffmann and Steinman): roughly 95-97% of animal species (all invertebrates) persist on innate immunity only, using pattern-recognition receptors/TLRs, antimicrobial peptides, phagocytosis and melanization/encapsulation. Innate-only immunity is a proven viable design at small body size, short lifespan and high fecundity — the counterweight the reasoner must reconcile with the SCID evidence.

Trained immunity (Netea et al., 2011 onward; consolidated review-stage ~2016): innate cells (monocytes, NK cells) carry epigenetically-encoded, non-antigen-specific memory, e.g. BCG-induced heterologous protection. Innate immunity is therefore not strictly memoryless — the documented substrate for any 'vaccine-like' technology (thread 2), which would be broad, short-lived immunostimulation rather than pathogen-specific priming.

Convergent 'adaptive-like' immunity via Variable Lymphocyte Receptors in jawless vertebrates - Pancer & Cooper et al., Nature 2004 (sea lamprey) and PNAS 2005 (hagfish): a fully independent, LRR-based (non-immunoglobulin) somatically-diversified anticipatory receptor system. Documents that adaptive immunity can be re-invented on a different molecular chassis; bounds the 'what would replace it' thread.

Cancer immunoediting/immunosurveillance - Burnet-Thomas hypothesis (1957); Dunn, Old & Schreiber formalization (Nature Immunology 2002); Schreiber, Old & Smyth (Science 2011); checkpoint-blockade validation (Allison & Honjo, 2018 Nobel): adaptive T cells surveil tumors, and adaptive-immunodeficient hosts (transplant recipients, AIDS) show an elevated but SELECTIVE cancer excess — predominantly virally-driven and highly-immunogenic tumors, not a uniform rise across all cancers; NK-based innate surveillance persists. Constrains thread (5) against the naive 'cancer explosion' answer.

Maternal-fetal tolerance depends on adaptive immune modulation — regulatory T-cell expansion (Aluvihare, Kallikourdis & Betz, Nature Immunology 2004), trophoblast HLA-G, and IDO-mediated tryptophan catabolism (Munn & Mellor, Science 1998): eutherian placental pregnancy tolerates the semi-allogeneic fetus largely via adaptive mechanisms. It is already known that the fetal-tolerance 'problem' is itself created by adaptive immunity — directly relevant to thread (4).

Allergy, asthma and classical autoimmune disease are adaptive-immune diseases: IgE-mediated type-I hypersensitivity (Ishizaka & Ishizaka 1966; independently Johansson & Bennich 1967; class named IgE 1968) and self-reactive-lymphocyte disorders (type-1 diabetes, MS, RA, SLE). Settled immunology well before 2020: without B/T cells these disease categories cannot exist in their known forms — the obvious first-order deduction for thread (7), which therefore scores low on novelty on its own.

Allograft rejection is adaptive/MHC-driven - Medawar's acquired-tolerance work (1940s-50s; 1960 Nobel): acute transplant rejection is T-cell/MHC-restricted. Removing adaptive immunity removes the dominant acute-rejection barrier, leaving only innate/NK 'missing-self' and complement barriers — the known first-order transplantation consequence (thread 3).

Herd immunity, influenza antigenic drift/shift, and 'original antigenic sin' (herd-immunity concept, 1920s-30s; standard influenza literature) all presuppose antibody-mediated adaptive immunity and the host-pathogen antibody arms race. It is already established that these epidemiological concepts are contingent on adaptive immunity (thread 8).

Peto's paradox (Peto, 1975; Caulin & Maley, Trends in Ecology & Evolution 2011): large, long-lived animals require enhanced cell-intrinsic somatic tumor suppression independent of immunity. Bears on whether an ~80-year, large-bodied, innate-only mammal is viable at all on the cancer axis (interaction of threads 1 and 5).

Innate antiviral defense (type-I interferon, NK cells, complement) operates independently of adaptive immunity, but long-term and latent viral control (herpesviruses, EBV, CMV) is strongly CD8 T-cell dependent (standard virology). Known that latent-virus containment would collapse without adaptive immunity — relevant to threads (1) and (8).
hard_rules: COHERENCE (category-constraint): the answer must hold the counterfactual fixed. No consequence may covertly reintroduce adaptive immunity — no antibodies, B/T cells, MHC-restricted presentation, or clonal antigen-specific memory anywhere. Any thread whose reasoning smuggles in 'the body would just make antibodies to X' is a rule violation and that consequence is disqualified. This is the single most common failure mode and MUST be checked line-by-line.

RETAINED SUBSTRATE: innate mechanisms explicitly listed in the prompt (phagocytes, complement, NK cells, TLR/PRR, type-I interferon, antimicrobial peptides, mucosal barriers, and documented epigenetic 'trained immunity') ARE available and may be invoked; invoking them is not a violation.

MECHANISTIC GROUNDING: every claimed downstream effect must name the specific innate or non-immune mechanism that produces it. Hand-waved effects with no named mechanism do not count toward New/Useful/Surprising.

EMPIRICAL ANCHORING: the answer must not contradict the two hard data points in the known-answers list simultaneously — it may not claim innate-only humans would be essentially healthy (SCID refutes this) NOR that they would instantly go extinct (invertebrates refute this). A passing answer must explicitly reconcile the SCID evidence with the invertebrate evidence (e.g., via body-size/lifespan/fecundity/pathogen-load trade-offs).

CROSS-THREAD CONSISTENCY: the world must be globally consistent. At minimum, the survival-to-reproduction claim (thread 1) must be numerically/logically compatible with the demographic strategy invoked (r- vs K-selection) and with the cancer claim (thread 5). At least one explicit cross-thread interaction must be worked out.

SCORING GATE (CREST all-three rule): the item counts as creative only if New AND Useful AND Surprising each clear threshold. Because this item isolates SURPRISE, restating any entry in the dated known-answers list scores low on New by construction; the discriminating signal is whether the counterintuitive consequences (and their mechanistic defense) exceed the expert baseline below.
expert_baseline: A well-read immunologist given an afternoon would produce approximately the following, and a submission must EXCEED it to score Surprising. (1) Lethality: cite SCID/David Vetter — innate-only modern humans die of infection in infancy under normal exposure — but temper with the invertebrate and trained-immunity evidence; conclude the K-selected human life-history (large body, long childhood, few offspring, ~80-yr lifespan) is probably incompatible with innate-only immunity at current pathogen loads, so the species would have to be radically more fecund (r-selected) with a much shorter effective lifespan. (2) Vaccination: impossible in the antibody/memory sense; the only substitute is trained-immunity-style broad, short-lived, non-specific immunostimulation (BCG-like). (3) Transplantation: MUCH easier — acute T-cell/MHC rejection gone; only innate/NK 'missing-self' and complement barriers remain. (4) Pregnancy: the semi-allograft tolerance problem is created BY adaptive immunity (Treg/HLA-G/IDO), so with no adaptive immunity there is no adaptive fetal rejection to suppress — placental pregnancy is likely immunologically EASIER, a point lay reasoners get backwards. (5) Cancer: loss of T-cell surveillance raises virally-driven/highly-immunogenic cancers (as in transplant/AIDS patients) but NOT all cancers uniformly; NK surveillance and Peto's-paradox cell-intrinsic suppression persist. (6) Microbiome: without secretory IgA the commensal community is governed only by antimicrobial peptides and innate barriers — a less-negotiated, more invasion-prone mucosal ecology. (7) Allergy/asthma/autoimmunity: simply gone (first-order, low-novelty). (8) Coevolution: no antigenic drift/shift arms race and no 'original antigenic sin'; pathogens optimize against conserved innate targets that are harder to escape, while latency strategies (herpesviruses) become far more lethal without T-cell containment; 'herd immunity' does not exist. (9) Medicine/society: no vaccination, serology, antibody diagnostics or antibody-based blood typing; medicine leans on antimicrobials, hygiene and immunostimulants; r-selected demography. The expert flags the transplantation-easy and pregnancy-easier findings as the 'clever' observations — so a Surprising submission must go BEYOND these to non-obvious third-order effects (e.g. pathogens shifting from antigenic-variation to innate-evasion/immunosuppression, reshaping which microbes dominate; collapse of transfusion medicine's antibody logic while complement/ABO-carbohydrate hyperacute reactions persist; trained-immunity set-points becoming epigenetically heritable and reshaping population susceptibility; or a slowed pathogen-evolution arms race stabilizing host-microbe relationships into obligate symbioses).

query: Suppose limited liability for equity owners had never existed anywhere in history. The only business forms are the sole proprietorship and the general partnership, and every owner bears unlimited, joint-and-several personal liability for all of the firm's debts and torts. A firm may still own property and be sued in its own name, but nothing ever caps an owner's downside at the amount invested. Everything else — technology, resources, geography, human nature — is as in our world. In non-obvious ways, how would this reshape the scale and financing of enterprise, securities markets, and the institutions that would arise to do the work limited liability does for us?
known_answers: 1911 — Nicholas Murray Butler (Columbia University) declared the limited-liability corporation 'the greatest single discovery of modern times,' asserting that even steam and electricity would be 'reduced to comparative impotence without it'; this frames the standard 'LL was essential to industrialization' thesis.

1985 & 1991 — Frank Easterbrook & Daniel Fischel ('Limited Liability and the Corporation,' Univ. of Chicago Law Review 1985; 'The Economic Structure of Corporate Law,' 1991) argue LL reduces shareholder monitoring costs, enables passive diversification, promotes liquid/homogeneous secondary markets, and lets managers take value-maximizing risk — implying that without LL there are no liquid mass equity markets and the cost of equity capital is far higher.

2000 — Henry Hansmann & Reinier Kraakman ('The Essential Role of Organizational Law,' Yale Law Journal) contend the legally ESSENTIAL contribution is ENTITY shielding / affirmative asset partitioning, NOT owner-shielding (limited liability), which they argue could in principle be replicated by private contract with voluntary creditors — implying the counterfactual world can partly self-heal for contract creditors, leaving tort creditors as the real bite.

1991 — Hansmann & Kraakman ('Toward Unlimited Shareholder Liability for Corporate Torts,' Yale Law Journal) identify externalized tort/environmental harm as LL's chief social cost and propose pro-rata unlimited shareholder liability for torts — implying a no-LL world internalizes tort/environmental costs.
2003 — Micklethwait & Wooldridge ('The Company: A Short History of a Revolutionary Idea') treat the joint-stock, limited-liability company as the foundation of modern capitalism and mass prosperity.

Dated legal record: UK Bubble Act 1720 (repealed 1825); New York 1811 general limited-liability manufacturing statute (called 'the world's first modern limited liability law'); UK Limited Liability Act 1855; Joint Stock Companies Act 1856; Companies Act 1862 (extended to insurers); Salomon v A Salomon & Co Ltd (1897, separate legal personality); German GmbH statute 1892; UK Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2000.

Empirical partial-counterfactuals (dated): City of Glasgow Bank failure 1878 ruined unlimited-liability shareholders and prompted the Companies Act 1879 permitting banks to adopt limited/reserve liability; U.S. national banks carried 'double liability' from the National Banking Act 1863 until the New Deal banking reforms wound it down in stages (Banking Act of 1933 s.22 ended it for shares issued after 16 June 1933; national banks could terminate it on existing shares from 1935; full statutory abolition 1953); California's constitution imposed proportionate unlimited shareholder liability from 1849 (Const. 1849 s.36, carried into Art. XII s.3 of the 1879 Constitution) until the amendment repealing it was adopted 4 November 1930, with the implementing Civil Code s.322 repeal effective 14 August 1931; Lloyd's of London 'Names' bore unlimited personal liability until the asbestos/pollution (APH) losses of the 1988-1992 years of account forced limited-liability corporate members to be admitted in 1994, followed by the Reconstruction & Renewal plan (1995) and the transfer of all pre-1993 liabilities to Equitas in September 1996; American Express operated as an unlimited-liability joint-stock association until 1965.

1990s-2000s — Naomi Lamoreaux and related business-history scholarship show partnership forms persisted and financed substantial 19th-century enterprise, with the corporation's advantage widening only as capital intensity and ownership dispersion rose (a check on claims that no large firms could form at all).

Standard pre-cutoff finance theory that bounds naive answers: Modigliani-Miller (1958) capital-structure irrelevance under frictionless markets (blocks the claim that a costless equity-to-debt substitution occurs); Markowitz portfolio selection (1952), which shows why unlimited joint-and-several liability destroys small-investor diversification (each added holding adds unbounded tail risk rather than reducing variance).

Critical literature argues limited liability enables negative corporate externalities through risk-shifting; a distinct libertarian strand (e.g. Rothbard) instead accepts owner-shielding as a contractual matter between the firm and its VOLUNTARY creditors while denying that tort liability to third parties can be contracted away. Either way, the aggregate magnitude of these externalities is contested and not precisely quantified in the literature.

The 'obvious' consequence set already stated across popular and textbook treatments (and therefore NOT New if merely restated): firms would be smaller; capital pooling would be harder; stock markets would be thin or absent; there would be more family firms, state ownership, cooperatives and mutuals; heavier reliance on debt and retained earnings; slower or state-led railroad and heavy-industry development; ownership concentrated among the wealthy who can bear unlimited risk.
hard_rules: R1 Premise fidelity: no owner-shielding may reappear under any name. If the agent invokes any vehicle (trust, mutual, cooperative, syndicate, 'double liability'), it must show owners still face UNBOUNDED downside, or explicitly flag it as a partial workaround — not silently restore the thing removed. Entity shielding IS permitted by the premise; conflating entity shielding with owner shielding is a violation.

R2 Historical accuracy of partial-counterfactuals: the answer must not misstate the record. It must NOT claim railroads/canals were never built (early UK railways and canals were built under charter with unlimited or ambiguous liability); must NOT claim Lloyd's 'Names' had limited liability before the 1990s; must NOT date a UK general limited-liability regime before 1855 or New York's before 1811; must NOT claim U.S. bank 'double liability' was abolished before the 1930s.

R3 Economic-identity consistency: cannot violate accounting identities or well-established results. Claiming a costless shift from equity to debt is disallowed (must engage Modigliani-Miller frictions). Claiming small investors 'would just diversify normally' is disallowed — unlimited joint-and-several liability makes each added holding add unbounded tail risk, which breaks Markowitz-style diversification.

R4 Causal traceability: every consequence must be linked by an explicit mechanism to the removal of owner-shielding. A consequence that would occur regardless of limited liability, with no liability-linked mechanism, is out of scope and earns no credit.

R5 Ceteris paribus: technology, natural resources, geography, and human nature are held fixed. A consequence may not be 'explained' by positing different physics, a different resource endowment, or a benevolent world-government not implied by the premise.

R6 Tort-vs-contract asymmetry must be respected: voluntary (contract) creditors can accept negotiated liability caps, so the sharpest bite falls on involuntary/tort creditors and on passive equity investors. An answer that treats all creditors identically has missed the constrained structure of the counterfactual.
expert_baseline: A competent but conventional domain expert would answer roughly as follows. (1) Enterprise scale/financing: truly large capital-intensive firms would be rarer and, where they exist, financed by (a) very wealthy individuals and dynastic families able to bear unlimited risk, (b) the state (state railroads, national champions, arsenals), or (c) asset-secured debt rather than dispersed equity. Railroads and heavy industry would tilt toward state or municipal ownership (the continental-European pattern) or toward a handful of tycoon-controlled partnerships; semiconductors, pharma, and frontier-AI compute — extremely capital- and tail-risk-intensive — would be disproportionately state-funded or confined to a few deep-pocketed sponsors, and their growth would be slower and more concentrated. (2) Securities markets: no mass retail equity culture. Because holding a share exposes the owner's entire personal wealth to the firm's liabilities, ordinary savers cannot safely hold — let alone diversify across — equities, since each added holding adds unbounded tail risk rather than reducing variance (Easterbrook-Fischel; Markowitz). Equity would be illiquid, closely held, and carry a large risk premium; secondary markets would be thin. Household saving would flow to bank deposits, bonds, annuities, and state savings vehicles. (3) Substitutes: the expert names liability insurance, contractual liability caps for voluntary creditors (Hansmann-Kraakman), mutual/cooperative and state ownership, and reputation/relationship finance (family networks, keiretsu/zaibatsu-style cross-holding, guarantor chains); the most likely dominant substitutes are a much larger insurance sector (insuring one's personal downside being the natural hedge) and the state as residual risk-bearer for large projects. (4) Second-order (state + wealth distribution + retirement): the state's economic footprint would be substantially larger (more state enterprise; more pay-as-you-go state pensions, since there is no mass funded-equity retirement system and thus no 401(k)/equity-cult). Wealth would be more concentrated in the risk-bearing owner class and a broad shareholding middle class would never form. With owners personally liable for torts, environmental and product-safety externalities would be more internalized, plausibly yielding more cautious risk-taking and cleaner but slower industry. This baseline is mostly first-order; a Surprising answer must exceed it — e.g., insurers becoming the de facto capital market and dominant financial institutions; contractual liability caps evolving into a shadow-corporate regime so the counterfactual partially self-heals for contract creditors while the judgment-proof problem for torts nearly vanishes; the venture-capital limited-partner structure (and hence the modern startup ecosystem) never forming, rerouting innovation through corporate labs and the state and reshaping the geography of innovation; or unlimited-liability equity partnership pushing mainstream finance toward Islamic-finance-style profit-and-loss-sharing norms.

query: Consider an Earth-like planet identical to ours in every way — air, chemistry, material strengths and densities, propellant performance, and all physical constants — except that surface gravity is fixed at 1.5 g (about 14.7 m/s^2). A human-scale species evolved there and built a spacefaring civilization under that gravity. Holding 1.5 g fixed everywhere, how would their engineering diverge from ours across access to space, large civil structures, and fluid, thermal, and power systems? Go past the obvious 'everything is 50% heavier' scaling to the non-obvious regime shifts — where higher gravity flips which technology wins or which design is even feasible, and where some quantity turns out to be counterintuitively gravity-invariant.
hard_rules: g' = 1.5 g0 (14.7 m/s^2) must be applied consistently in every calculation and every domain; an answer may not silently revert to 1 g where it is inconvenient, nor 'explain away' the gravity by changing the planet's mass, radius, atmosphere, materials, or chemistry.

All non-gravity physics is held at real Earth values: air density and composition, speed of sound, material densities and strengths (e.g., structural steel yield ~250-550 MPa, concrete, CFRP), and chemical-propellant specific impulse (LOX/LH2 vacuum Isp <= ~465 s (flown ceiling: RL10B-2 = 465.5 s), i.e. exhaust velocity v_e <= ~4.6 km/s). Any consequence that tacitly requires stronger materials, thinner/denser air, or higher-energy chemistry is DISQUALIFIED.

Launch/aerospace claims must be consistent with the Tsiolkovsky equation Delta-v = v_e ln(m0/mf) using realistic chemical Isp: at fixed radius, orbital velocity scales as sqrt(g') (~1.22x) and gravity losses rise, so Delta-v to LEO increases from ~9.5 km/s to roughly 12-13 km/s and the required propellant mass ratio grows EXPONENTIALLY (from ~8-9 to ~15-20 for hydrolox). Any claim of easy chemical single-stage-to-orbit at 1.5 g is invalid.

Structural claims must respect square-cube scaling and real material limits: the self-weight-limited maximum height of a given structural system scales as 1/g (~0.67x Earth for gravity-load-governed structures). An answer MUST distinguish gravity-load-governed structures (shorter/stouter) from wind- or seismic-governed structures (which scale differently), rather than asserting a blanket 0.67x on everything.

Fluid-statics and energy claims must respect linear-in-g scaling: hydrostatic pressure at depth (rho*g*h), pump head work, gravitational potential storage, buoyant force, and hydropower energy per unit volume per unit head all scale ~1.5x; natural-convection driving force (Grashof/Rayleigh number) scales with g, so buoyancy-driven passive cooling gets STRONGER, not weaker.

Space-elevator / tether claims must respect that the required tether taper ratio grows roughly exponentially with g for a fixed material strength; therefore with Earth-identical materials a space elevator is HARDER at 1.5 g, not a free escape from the rocket penalty. Getting this direction backwards violates the rules.
Conservation of energy and momentum and the laws of thermodynamics hold; no consequence may imply a perpetual-motion machine, over-unity storage, or free energy.
A consequence asserted as 'surprising' scores ZERO unless it is physically coherent under all rules above; incoherent novelty does not count as creative.
SCOPE: the species is fully adapted to 1.5 g; physiological 'the crew would be crushed' / biological-limit answers are out of scope — only engineering divergence is graded.
known_answers: Galileo, Two New Sciences (1638) / square-cube law: a structure's weight grows as volume (L^3) while load-bearing cross-section grows as area (L^2), so the maximum self-supporting height of a column/structure of a given material scales as 1/g. KNOWN since 1638 — no New credit for merely restating 'higher gravity means shorter, stouter structures.'

Tsiolkovsky rocket equation (published 1903; first derived by W. Moore, 1810-13) and the 'tyranny of the rocket equation': Delta-v = v_e ln(m0/mf); reaching LEO needs ~9.4-9.7 km/s including gravity and drag losses; wet mass grows exponentially with required Delta-v. KNOWN since 1903.

Michael Hippke, 'Spaceflight from Super-Earths is difficult,' Int. J. Astrobiology 18 (2019), arXiv:1804.04727 (submitted Apr 2018): required propellant mass is an EXPONENTIAL function of surface gravity; chemical rockets remain (barely) viable only up to ~10 Earth masses (a few g), and higher-gravity worlds need nuclear or non-chemical propulsion (e.g., an Apollo-class 45 t payload from a 10-Earth-mass world would need on the order of ~400,000 t (Hippke's telescope case is JWST at 6.2 t -> ~55,000 t; he does not discuss Hubble) of fuel). The headline 'rockets get exponentially harder with gravity, non-chemical propulsion needed' result is KNOWN as of 2018 — no Surprise credit for reaching only this conclusion.

Popular-science and worldbuilding treatments of high-gravity worlds (e.g., Randall Munroe's What If?, and Universe Today / Nautilus / worldbuilding essays, ~2012-2023): under higher gravity, buildings and trees are shorter and stockier, skeletons and legs thicker, flight harder, and spaceflight harder. These are the widely-circulated 'obvious' first-order consequences and are KNOWN as of ~2012-2023.

Aerospace-medicine literature on g-tolerance (20th century onward): acute human tolerance to sudden-onset +Gz is ~4-6 g before loss of consciousness (unpressurised, untrained), rising to 12-14 g for trained pilots in g-suits performing anti-g straining (Burton 1988); sustained MODERATE hypergravity (2-5 g) is poorly characterised, and no lethal-boundary magnitude for sustained acceleration is established in the literature (Eiband, NASA Memo 5-19-59E, 1959). KNOWN, and bounded here because the evolved species is stipulated adapted to 1.5 g.

Biomechanical scaling (McMahon's elastic-similarity paper, Science 1973; and separately R. McN. Alexander's work on locomotor scaling): limb and structural proportions scale with body size and gravity; higher g favours proportionally thicker limbs/columns. KNOWN since the 1970s.

Standard aerodynamics (textbook): lift and drag depend on air density, speed and wing area, NOT on gravity; therefore at a fixed atmosphere a 1.5x-heavier aircraft needs 1.5x lift -> higher wing loading, faster takeoff/landing, longer runways and more thrust, but the air itself is unchanged. KNOWN.

Aerostatics / Archimedes (textbook): buoyant lift = (rho_air - rho_gas) * g * V and vehicle weight also scale with g, so the float condition of a lighter-than-air craft is gravity-INVARIANT — a balloon that floats on Earth still floats at 1.5 g. KNOWN, and a standard 'gotcha' invariant.

Launcher staging and reusability economics (SpaceX-era analyses, 2010s): staging benefit and the payload penalty of reusability are Delta-v-driven; higher Delta-v budgets push toward more staging and away from reuse. KNOWN as of the 2010s.

Space-elevator engineering (Pearson 1975; Edwards 2000s): required tether taper ratio depends exponentially on rho*g*R / material strength, so a space elevator is only marginal with Earth's best real materials at 1 g. The scaling with g is KNOWN — an agent gets no New credit for the taper-ratio formula itself, only for correctly propagating it to the counterfactual.
expert_baseline: FIRST-ORDER BASELINE a competent engineering panel would produce WITHOUT deep research (this is the reference against which Surprise is judged). DOMAIN 1 (space/aero): At fixed radius, orbital velocity scales as sqrt(1.5)=1.22x (Earth LEO ~7.8 -> ~9.5 km/s) and gravity losses rise, so Delta-v to LEO climbs from ~9.5 to very roughly 12-13 km/s. Via Tsiolkovsky at hydrolox v_e~4.4 km/s, the mass ratio jumps from ~8.7 (e^2.16) to ~17-19 (e^2.85-2.95): chemical SSTO is impossible, heavy multi-staging is mandatory, payload fractions collapse, and reusability (already a Delta-v/payload tax) becomes even less affordable — so their early space age favours expendable, many-stage vehicles and pushes toward higher-Isp (nuclear-thermal) propulsion far earlier (consistent with Hippke). Winged flight: air is unchanged, so a 1.5x-heavier aircraft needs 1.5x lift -> higher wing loading, higher takeoff/landing speeds, longer runways, more installed thrust; harder but not qualitatively impossible. Lighter-than-air: float condition is gravity-invariant, so balloons/airships work the same. DOMAIN 2 (civil): square-cube gives self-weight-limited max height ~0.67x Earth for gravity-governed structures; towers stubbier with heavier columns and more material per floor; long-span bridges see dead load dominate sooner, so max spans shrink and decks thicken (shorter, more numerous spans); dams face 1.5x hydrostatic load -> thicker gravity dams; foundations/geotech carry 1.5x load with worse settlement and slope stability -> deeper/wider foundations, more landslides. DOMAIN 3 (fluids/thermal): pumping water to a given height costs 1.5x energy (static head ∝ g); hydropower and pumped/solid-mass gravity storage yield 1.5x energy per unit height (relatively MORE attractive); turbomachinery cores are pressure-dominated and change little (a 'least-changed' candidate); tribology worsens as self-weight normal forces and thus friction/wear/rolling-resistance rise ~1.5x. RANKED JUDGEMENT (baseline): MOST changed = launch-vehicle / access-to-space engineering (exponential sensitivity to g). LEAST changed = pressure-driven internal flows, gas-turbine cores, and lighter-than-air buoyancy (gravity-invariant ratio). The baseline STOPS at these linear/exponential per-domain scalings and the single invariant.
