It generally does NOT surface the cross-domain regime shifts that constitute Surprise here, e.g.: (a) natural-convection cooling GETS STRONGER with g (Rayleigh ∝ g) while active pumping gets costlier, so the optimal thermal-management architecture flips toward passive thermosiphons and natural-draft towers — a fluids×structures coupling; (b) because the space-elevator taper ratio grows ~exponentially with g at fixed real materials, the elevator is HARDER not easier, so non-tether escape (mass drivers up mountains, air-breathing/spaceplane assist, nuclear) becomes the mainline path — a reversal naive reasoning gets backwards; (c) winged/air-breathing access degrades only ~linearly while rockets degrade exponentially, so their access-to-space stays air-breathing-dominated far longer and their spaceplane lineage diverges sharply from ours; (d) the aerostatic invariance plus the exponential rocket penalty makes balloon/rockoon and high-altitude-platform launch assist structurally central to their program rather than a novelty; (e) gravity-based grid storage (hydro, pumped, solid-mass) is uniformly ~1.5x denser, reshaping their entire energy-storage economics toward gravity and away from chemistry.
author_expected_surprises: A high-Surprise answer must reach coherent cascades of this second/third-order kind, not merely the per-domain 1.5x factors.

query: Suppose the statute of limitations — and every functional equivalent, including statutes of repose, laches, and adverse-possession and prescription doctrines — had never developed in any legal system. Any claim, civil or criminal, has always been filable at any time, however many decades or centuries have passed, and lapse of time alone has never barred a right or ripened one. Hold the rest of legal, economic, and social history as close to ours as coherence allows. In non-obvious ways, how would this world diverge — across evidence and fact-finding, long-tail liability, property title, historical-injustice claims, record-keeping, and the social need for closure — and what mechanisms would evolve to do the work that time-bars do for us?
known_answers: c. 450 BCE - 3rd c. CE (Roman law): Time-based extinction/acquisition of claims is ~2,000 years old — usucapio in the Twelve Tables and later longi temporis praescriptio; civil-law 'prescription' (extinctive and acquisitive) descends from this. KNOWN: the premise diverges from Roman law forward, so any credible answer must reckon with the fact that no major legal tradition has ever actually lacked a time-bar.

Classical Anglo-American doctrine (maxim vigilantibus non dormientibus jura subveniunt; Wood v. Carpenter, 101 U.S. 135 (1879); Justice Jackson in Order of Railroad Telegraphers v. Ry. Express Agency, 321 U.S. 342 (1944)): the three canonical rationales for statutes of limitations are (a) evidence decays (witnesses die, memories fade, documents are lost), (b) defendants deserve 'repose'/peace, and (c) plaintiffs should be diligent. KNOWN: reciting these three rationales as the 'consequences of removal' earns no novelty.

Pre-cutoff, well-known: our world ALREADY contains large no-time-bar zones — murder has no statute of limitations in most U.S. states and many countries, and the 1968 UN Convention on the Non-Applicability of Statutory Limitations to War Crimes and Crimes Against Humanity (in force 1970) makes genocide/war crimes/crimes against humanity non-prescriptible. KNOWN: these are live natural experiments; an answer that claims no-SOL claims are simply unadjudicable is contradicted by routine cold-case murder prosecutions.

2002-2023 (documented): revival/abolition of limitations for child sexual abuse — e.g., California AB 218 (2019) and New York Child Victims Act (2019) 'look-back windows' — produced a surge of decades-old claims, drove Catholic dioceses and the Boy Scouts of America (Ch. 11, 2020) into bankruptcy, and triggered acute long-tail insurance-coverage disputes. KNOWN: this is the closest real mini-experiment in 'no SOL' effects on institutions and insurers.

1970s-2000s (documented): asbestos and environmental (CERCLA/Superfund, 1980) litigation are the textbook long-tail problem — claims surfacing decades after exposure created retroactive mass liabilities, insurer insolvencies, and 'occurrence' vs 'claims-made' coverage wars. KNOWN: the insurance industry's basic vulnerability to unbounded tails is well documented.

Law-and-economics literature (e.g., T. Merrill, 'Property Rules, Liability Rules, and Adverse Possession,' 1985; Posner, Economic Analysis of Law): adverse possession and prescriptive easements function as title-clearing/quieting devices that reward productive use and eliminate stale claims. KNOWN: the efficiency rationale for time-ripening of title is standard.

1858 forward (Torrens system, South Australia) and recording-act jurisdictions: title-certainty machinery (curtain/mirror/indemnity principles) and the title-insurance industry already exist precisely to manage the risk of old, undiscovered claims. KNOWN: a naive answer that 'invents' title registries as a novel adaptation is reciting an existing institution.

Reparations/historical-injustice case law: SOL and laches are already the primary doctrinal barrier — In re African-American Slave Descendants Litigation, 471 F.3d 754 (7th Cir. 2006) (dismissed partly on limitations); Mau Mau claims against the UK settled June 2013; Herero/Nama claims against Germany; Holocaust-era art, addressed by the U.S. HEAR Act (Pub. L. 114-308, 16 Dec 2016), which PREEMPTS state SOLs and substitutes a uniform federal 6-year period running from ACTUAL DISCOVERY rather than abolishing the time-bar. KNOWN: that removing SOL would 'open the door' to these suits is the obvious first move; the non-obvious question is what binds after the door opens.

Transitional-justice literature (South Africa TRC, 1995-2003 (Act No. 34 of 1995; core HRV hearings 1996-1998; Amnesty Committee ran on, work formally ended March 2003); amnesty-vs-prosecution debates): 'closure' can be produced by truth commissions, amnesties, and reconciliation rather than by the clock. KNOWN: pointing at truth commissions as a closure substitute is already in the literature.

General doctrinal fact (pre-cutoff): even where SOL is absent or waived, claims are still gated by OTHER doctrines — sovereign immunity, act-of-state, standing, non-retroactivity of substantive law, causation, and burden of proof. KNOWN: this 'other gatekeepers still exist' point is standard and must be engaged rather than presented as a discovery.
expert_baseline: A legal expert would predict the obvious first-order effects: without time-bars, courts face a flood of stale claims where evidence has decayed (lost witnesses, destroyed records, faded memory), making fact-finding unreliable and leaving defendants and title-holders perpetually exposed. The convergent expert answer is that the evidentiary and repose work done by time-bars is reassigned to procedural substitutes: heightened burdens of proof and adverse-inference/spoliation rules for old claims, mandatory long-horizon record retention, expanded liability insurance to price indefinite exposure, and stronger Torrens-style title registration to quiet property, with closure shifted onto truth-commission and amnesty mechanisms. This baseline stops at 'evidence decays, so compensate with proof rules and insurance';
hard_rules: PREMISE FIXITY: The answer may not reintroduce any temporal bar under another name. No laches, repose, prescription, or adverse possession may be used as a background fact. A time-like effect is permitted ONLY if it is explicitly derived as an EVOLVED SUBSTITUTE the counterfactual world produces (e.g., evidentiary decay, contractual release) and is labeled as such — not assumed.

NO SMUGGLING THE REAL RULE: The answer must not assert 'claims would of course be dismissed after X years' as a given. Any dismissal of an old claim must be justified by a mechanism the counterfactual world actually evolves (burden of proof, immunity, contract), never by an unstated limitations period.

CETERIS PARIBUS: Facts not causally downstream of the premise stay as in our world. The agent may not alter unrelated institutions (form of government, existence of insurance, DNA forensics, etc.) except as a derived consequence of the premise.

VALID CAUSAL CHAINS: Every claimed consequence must trace back to 'lapse of time no longer bars claims' through stated intermediate steps. No non-sequiturs; each cross-domain link must name the transmitting mechanism.
ORDER-OF-EFFECT STRUCTURE: The response must actually separate first-order from second-/third-order effects in each of the six domains. Lumping everything as first-order fails.

CONSISTENCY WITH NATURAL EXPERIMENTS: Because our world already has no-SOL zones (murder, genocide, revived CSA windows, asbestos long-tail), the answer must be consistent with what those show. It may not claim no-SOL claims are impossible to adjudicate (cold-case murders are prosecuted) nor that removal has no institutional cost (dioceses/BSA bankruptcies show otherwise). It must engage these, not ignore them.

COVERAGE FLOOR (for the Useful score): all six domains addressed + at least two evolved substitute mechanisms + at least three explicit, mechanism-named cross-domain links + an explicit convergence-vs-divergence verdict with a defense.

NOVELTY BAR (for the New score): points that merely restate items on the dated known-answers list (the three canonical SOL rationales, 'title registries would exist,' 'truth commissions provide closure,' 'other doctrines still gate claims') earn no novelty credit; New is judged against that list.
author_expected_surprises: it would not anticipate the deeper second-order effects, such as how a heightened burden of proof for stale claims silently re-creates a probabilistic, evidence-based time-bar, or how indefinite liability reshapes the economics of long-lived firms and asset ownership.

query: Imagine a universe with identical quantum mechanics and thermodynamics, except that condensed matter can never form long-range periodic (crystalline) order — every solid is frozen into an amorphous, glassy state with short-range order only, no lattice or unit cell ever forming. Nothing else about atoms, bonds, or the laws of physics changes. Trace the mechanism-linked consequences for materials across structure determination, electronics and computing, catalysis, structural metals, magnetism and energy, and the phase behavior of water and ice. Reach for the most surprising, non-obvious second- and third-order effects — including cases where losing crystallinity turns out to be a net benefit.
known_answers: COMPILED 2026-07-29; all cited facts predate the training cutoff and are single-source-retrievable, so restating them counts as KNOWN (not New/Surprising).
Crystalline solids have long-range periodic order; glasses/amorphous solids have only short-range order (nearest-neighbor coordination without a repeating lattice).

X-ray crystallography determines atomic structure via Bragg diffraction from a periodic lattice; it required crystals and underpinned 20th-century structural chemistry and structural biology (e.g., the DNA double helix from fiber diffraction, hemoglobin/myoglobin). Non-crystalline structure methods are cryo-EM, solution/solid-state NMR, and pair-distribution-function (PDF) / EXAFS local-structure analysis.

Single-crystal silicon is the substrate for high-performance CMOS logic; hydrogenated amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) has low electron field-effect/drift mobility (~1 cm2/V.s) and is used in solar cells and legacy LCD TFT backplanes.

Amorphous oxide semiconductors, notably a-IGZO (indium-gallium-zinc-oxide, Nomura et al., Nature 432, 488 (2004), from Hosono's group), reach mobility ~10 cm2/V.s (roughly 10x a-Si:H) and are the industry TFT backplane for high-resolution/OLED displays - direct proof that working transistors do NOT strictly require crystals.

Light-emitting diodes and laser diodes require crystalline direct-gap semiconductors (GaN, GaAs) with sharp band edges; amorphous semiconductors exhibit Urbach band tails and localized states below a mobility edge (Anderson localization), which suppress efficient radiative recombination and lasing.

Zeolites and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are crystalline microporous solids whose shape-selective catalysis and molecular-sieve separations depend on precise, periodic pore geometry; fluid catalytic cracking and xylene isomerization in refining use zeolite catalysts. Amorphous silica-alumina was the pre-zeolite cracking catalyst and is far less shape-selective.

Bulk metallic glasses (e.g., Zr-based Vitreloy) have very high yield strength and large elastic limits but poor tensile ductility, failing by localized shear banding with negligible work hardening; crystalline metals get ductility, toughness, and work hardening from dislocation glide on lattice slip planes.

Permanent (hard) magnets such as Nd2Fe14B and SmCo derive coercivity from the high magnetocrystalline anisotropy of specific crystalline phases; amorphous ferromagnets (Fe-based 'metglas') are magnetically SOFT (low coercivity/anisotropy) and are prized for low-loss transformer cores.

Piezoelectricity, pyroelectricity, and ferroelectricity require non-centrosymmetric crystal structures; quartz crystal oscillators provide the frequency reference for nearly all modern electronics. Poled semicrystalline polymers (PVDF) and poled glasses show piezo/pyroelectric response via frozen-in oriented dipoles rather than lattice symmetry.
Lithium-ion cathodes (layered LiCoO2, spinel LiMn2O4, olivine LiFePO4) are crystalline intercalation hosts enabling reversible topotactic Li insertion/extraction.
Single-crystal nickel-base superalloy turbine blades eliminate grain boundaries to resist high-temperature creep in jet engines and gas turbines.

Crystalline ice Ih (~0.917 g/cm3) is less dense than liquid water and floats because of its open hydrogen-bonded lattice; amorphous ices exist as low-density (LDA, ~0.94 g/cm3) and high-density (HDA, ~1.15-1.17 g/cm3) forms (with medium-density MDA, ~1.06 g/cm3, reported 2023).
Conventional BCS superconductivity occurs in some amorphous/disordered metals; high-Tc cuprate and iron-pnictide superconductivity requires specific crystalline layered structures.

Nonlinear-optical frequency conversion and electro-optic modulation use non-centrosymmetric crystals (KDP, LiNbO3, BBO, KTP); silica optical fiber is an amorphous glass and carries the internet via chi(3) (Kerr/Raman) effects, with weak chi(2) obtainable only by poling.

Structural color and photonic bandgaps in opals and many butterfly wings arise from periodic nanostructure; some amorphous nanostructures (e.g., certain bird feathers) produce non-iridescent structural color.

Solid-state electronic theory is built on Bloch's theorem, band structure, and Brillouin zones, all of which presuppose a periodic potential; disordered solids are instead described by Anderson localization, mobility edges, and Mott's ideas.
expert_baseline: All metals are metallic glasses: very hard and high-strength but brittle, with no dislocation-mediated ductility or work hardening, so structural engineering moves away from formable steels. Semiconductors still exist but only in amorphous form, so high-performance single-crystal-silicon CMOS is impossible; devices resemble slow, leaky a-Si-quality electronics, and sharp-band-edge LEDs/laser diodes and single-crystal quartz oscillators are unavailable. X-ray crystallography is impossible, so atomic structures must be inferred from spectroscopy or glass diffraction. Zeolite and MOF shape-selective catalysis and molecular sieving are gone; catalysis falls back on amorphous high-surface-area supports. Water ice is glassy rather than hexagonal. Net picture: harder but more brittle materials, degraded electronics, and a chemistry that never gets its crystallographic photograph of the atom.' Note this baseline is almost entirely a list of LOSSES, is roughly one arena deep, and treats each arena in isolation.
hard_rules: SINGLE-TOGGLE DISCIPLINE: only the stated premise (no long-range crystalline/periodic order; short-range order permitted) may change. All other physics and chemistry - quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, bond energies, atomic properties, the second law, conservation laws - are held fixed. Every consequence must be a forced entailment of the premise, not a smuggled extra assumption.

MECHANISM REQUIRED: each consequence must state the causal chain premise -> altered material property -> altered material/technology. Free-associated outcomes with no mechanistic link are invalid and must not be scored as creative.

NO SMUGGLED CRYSTALS: the answer may not invoke any crystalline material as a workaround (no zeolites, MOFs, single-crystal Si, GaN, quartz, NdFeB, LiCoO2, LiNbO3, single-crystal superalloys, ice Ih). Amorphous/short-range-ordered analogs that genuinely exist in our world MAY be invoked with correct properties: silica glass, bulk metallic glass, a-Si:H, a-IGZO, Fe-based metglas soft magnets, LDA/HDA glassy ice, amorphous silica-alumina catalysts, poled PVDF/glass, and PDF/EXAFS/NMR/cryo-EM structure methods.

RETAINED FACTS MUST BE CORRECT: any real-world material property cited (e.g., a-IGZO mobility >> a-Si:H; metallic glasses lack tensile ductility; magnetocrystalline anisotropy sources hard-magnet coercivity; silica fiber is a glass) must be factually accurate as of the dated known-answers list. A wrong retained fact invalidates that branch.

COVERAGE + DEPTH: must address all six named arenas AND surface at least four non-obvious second/third-order consequences that are absent from the expert baseline. Merely restating the known-answers list or the expert baseline scores New=low and Surprising=low by construction.

SYMMETRY-HONESTY: where the premise both destroys and enables, both directions must be reported. At minimum the answer must acknowledge cases where losing crystallinity is a NET BENEFIT (e.g., low-loss amorphous soft-magnetic transformer cores; glassy silica optical fiber already being the internet's medium; disappearance of pharmaceutical polymorphism). An answer that reports only losses is incomplete.

known_answers: Nicolas Rashevsky's 'organismic sets' and relational biology using n-ary relations (organismic sets ~1967; relational biology ~1954): the founding move of describing biological ORGANIZATION abstractly rather than by material composition. Robert Rosen's relational biology and (M,R)-systems (metabolism-repair): modeling organisms as mappings and their compositions inside small categories of sets, with 'closure to efficient causation' expressed through impredicative/self-referential maps (f: A->B together with a repair map that reconstructs f). CRITICAL for novelty scoring: composition, identity, representability, and the Yoneda lemma has been used ONCE in a peripheral corner of this lineage (Baianu, Bull. Math. Biophys. 35:213-218, 1973, applies Yoneda to constructing categories of generalized (M,R)-systems). Rosen himself never used it, Louie's monographs do not, and Loregian's categorical reconstruction (arXiv:2012.11648) does not. So 'metabolism as morphisms' is NOT new, but a Yoneda identification of a cell state with its perturbational-response functor is NOT foreclosed by this lineage.

Louie — 'More Than Life Itself' (2009) and 'The Reflection of Life' (Springer, 2013) — using categorical functional entailment; plus Letelier, Cardenas & Cornish-Bowden, J. Theor. The 'self-maintaining/self-repairing organism as a closed categorical object' mapping is therefore known.

Research program from ~1987; monograph 'Memory Evolutive Systems: Hierarchy, Emergence, Cognition' (2007). Colimits/limits and multi-scale hierarchy mapped onto biology are thus already claimed.

R1 (equivalence relation must be exact): The corporate operations assigned to the three Reidemeister moves must be EXACTLY the reorganizations that leave the claimed control invariant unchanged. If any proposed 'move' changes ultimate control, it is not a Reidemeister move and the mapping fails. The answer must state the induced equivalence relation on ownership diagrams explicitly.

R2 (invariant must be proven invariant): The quantity claimed to correspond to a knot invariant must be argued to be unchanged under ALL THREE 'Reidemeister' corporate operations — mirroring how Reidemeister-invariance is precisely what certifies a knot invariant. A bare correspondence table without an invariance argument fails.

R3 (orientation must be handled): Ownership edges are DIRECTED and WEIGHTED by share fraction; knot strands are unweighted 1-manifolds (they may carry an orientation, and orientation is required for crossing signs and linking number, but they admit no edge weight). The answer must explicitly resolve this mismatch (e.g., via oriented links and signed linking number, or by restricting to a sub-structure) or flag it as a bounding limitation. Silently treating ownership as an unoriented knot fails.

R4 (unknot / unknotting number): The 'unknot' must correspond to an acyclic control structure (a pure tree/pyramid with no circular shareholding). The unknotting number is the minimum number of CROSSING CHANGES (passing the knot through itself), not deletions; the answer must therefore either identify a corporate operation that is genuinely a crossing SWITCH (e.g. reversing which of two entities holds through the other) and count those, or state explicitly that the divestiture-count analogue is a different quantity (minimum feedback arc set / cycle-breaking edge cut) and not an unknotting number, and the answer must state whether this equals a known graph quantity (e.g., minimum feedback arc set / minimum cycle-breaking edge cut) rather than a genuine 3-dimensional unknotting number.

Producing a knot-flavored relabeling of the Vitali-Glattfelder-Battiston graph or the Brioschi-Buzzacchi-Colombo matrix without meeting this rule fails.

R6 (grounding): At least THREE concrete, named real-world instances must be tied to specific formal elements — e.g., a named keiretsu or chaebol circular-shareholding block, a named pyramidal business group, and a named antitrust- or regulator-mandated unwinding/divestiture. R7 (position against incumbents): The answer must cite and correctly characterize the existing formal apparatus for the target (the integrated-ownership control matrix (I - C)^{-1} and/or network-flow control) and state what the knot map adds or fails to add relative to it. Ignoring that a rigorous 'ultimate control' method already exists is an automatic fail.
